 Allerdings nicht so wie sich Rylee das vorgestellt hat, denn Coltons Damonen aus der Vergangenheit sind noch sehr prasent. 
 Beide mussen versuchen einen Weg zu finden aus alten Zwangen... 
 Cover

 Charaktere 
 Rylee Thomas ist eine ganz liebe, kann aber auch stur sein, was ihr aber nicht ganz so einfach fallt, denn Rylee ist sehr gefuhlvoll und mitfuhlend. 
 Colton Donovan hat Damonen aus seiner Vergangenheit und ist es gewohnt keinen in seine Nahe zu lassen und wenn dann nur zu seinen Bedingungen. 
 Schreibstil 
 Die Autorin K. Bromberg hat einen tollen flussigen Schreibstil der einen sehr schnell in den zweiten Teil entfuhrt der sehr viel uber die Beziehung der beiden verrat und man eine Achterbahn der Gefuhle erlebt. Bildhaft und emotional... ;) 
 Meinung 
 Wenn dich Deine Vergangenheit einholt.... 
 Dann sind wir bei Rylee und Colton angekommen, die sich von ihren Gefuhlen in einem Sturm befinden der nur die beiden zur Ruhe bringen konnen. 
 Aber Colton hat mit seinen inneren Damonen zu kampfen und schiebt Rylee von sich weg indem er ihr sagt dass er sie nur gebraucht hat und jetzt wegwirft wie ein altes Handtuch. 
 Aber Rylee lasst sich nachdem der erste Schock uberwunden ist nicht so behandeln und bekommt sehr schnell mit das vor ihr ein anderer Colton steht. 
 Nicht der taffe selbstsichere Geschaftsmann sondern ein kleiner Junge innerlich der tief verletzt wurde und nie uber diese Traumata hinweg kam. 
 Sie beschliesst ihm eine Chance zu geben und Colton muss sehr bald feststellen das diese Beziehung nicht auf seinen Regeln besteht sondern das hier nur ein miteinander herrschen kann.

 Unterstutzung und Zuspruch bekommt Rylee von Haddie die ihr mit Rat und Tat zur Seite steht, und somit beginnt fur beide eine Zeit in der sie beide aufeinander zugehen mussen.

Fueled is book #2 in K. Bromberg's trilogy. After screaming my head off because I didn't know that Driven ended with a massive cliffhanger I dove straight into this book and I was not disappointed!! In this book a lot of Colton's past conquests rear their ugly heads and cause Rylee to feel insecure about herself. We learn a lot more about the incidents from both Rylee and Colton's pasts. Can they overcome their own inner demons caused by their pasts to find a way to each other? This story spends a great deal of time focusing on the house that Rylee works with and I dare anyone who reads this book not to fall in love with all of the boys in the house, especially Zander. This poor boy has been traumatized so badly he doesn't speak and can barely interact with anyone. But Colton seems to be one person that Zander attaches himself to and the interactions between these two just melts your heart as well as Rylee's. 
 Fueled is a definite roller coaster ride of emotions and you go through hell and back with Rylee who has finally admitted her feelings for Colton. It's one step forward two steps back throughout this book. But man what a ride it is! Jealously and insecurities play a big part in this book. I will fully admit that I want to scratch the eyes right out of Tawny's head! Maybe right after I throat punch her! Tawny is an old friend of Colton's who he has dated in the past and now works for him. Trust me when you read these books you will want to do the same to her. 
 This book is a must read and one I will read over and over again along with Driven. I am so anxious for book #3 to come out!

Where do I begin? Fueled by K. Bromberg was the kind a book you want to crawl up with and get lost in. Rylee and Colton still do that thing they do. She pushes and he ends up pulling away. This is way more emotional then Driven. It will definitely hit that spot in your heart that you can't forget about. This time around Rylee is more accepting of Colton and his indiscretions. She wants to be with him and she is willing to accept the whole package. K. Bromberg definitely outdid herself, I didn't think it could possibly get better then Driven. I was wrong this book has blown me away! 
 First off if you haven't read book one in the series then stop here and go read it like right now. Fueled picks up exactly where Driven ended. Yes you have to experience that heart wrenching ending again, but it's all good. Rylee doesn't let Colton push her away this time. She goes back to him and gives him what he needs. What happens between them is simply beautiful. I can't even put into words the emotions I felt. I am still reeling from it and it's been a few weeks since I finished reading the book. In this book Rylee and Colton discover what they mean to one another. Rylee falls madly in love with Colton she is determined to show him in any way possible what he means to her. The only thing Colton knows is that he can't and won't let Rylee go. She drives him crazy, she makes him feel things he never thought possible. They are simply explosive together. It doesn't get better then what they have. Nothing is easy for them. They both have to work hard to be with one another. There are people determined to keep them a part. It seems Tawny is still in the picture. She is relentless when it comes to getting Colton's attention, and ylee isn't going to fight with all she has for Colton. I wouldn't expect anything less from Rylee. She is sweet and innocent on the outside, but on the inside her heart has had enough. She is a fighter and giving up is not an option. 
 I can't tell you enough how much I connected with this story and it's characters. This by far has to be one of the best books I have read this year. I feel so engrossed in this story that I can't stop thinking about how extraordinary the love between Rylee and Colton is. It makes me, happy, mad, and sad all at the same time. I am so in love with Rylee and Colton! I am invested in their happily ever after if ever one exists for them. 
 This is a must read. I want to shout from the rooftops for anyone to hear how wonderful this series is. I am so ready for the conclusion to their story. It can't come soon enough. My recommendation is a no brainer stop what your doing and get to it. You may have to join a support group for your ever huge book hangover. It will definitely be worth it though.

Colton outshines in this second installment of the Driven Trilogy by making a tremendous effort in his turbulent relationship with Rylee. He is courageous in the shadows of his creeping memories. He becomes a hero worth rooting for. 
 Rylee, on the other hand, is the sum of everything I despise in a leading lady. She's unattractively catty, immature, passive-aggressive, whimper-y, and avoids communication in lieu of running off her mouth. She doesn't listen. She runs away. Always running. Always whimpering. 
 The conflict is wholly based on a misunderstanding, made worse by Colton and Rylee's failure to discuss it. Would there have been a story if she'd just shut up and let him talk? No, but the constant relationship drama and the pages and pages of spiteful bickering keeps you engaged in a nerve-shredding, spit-flinging, positively frustrating way. Especially when you already know how things will end. You'll predict the cliffhanger chapters in advance. Everything about this story is predictable, because there's nothing unique here. 
 But I loved it. When I was forced to put the book down, I did so relunctantly. Maybe it's the evocative way it's written. Maybe it's all the raw heat blazing between Colton and Rylee, and the hot, hot, scorching hot sex scenes. Maybe it's the merciless drive to screw with your emotions until you're ready to become a beserker right along with the characters. Whatever it is, it puts you through the wringer and turns you into a glutton for more messy emotional chaos. 
 So, while this book is a compilation of all my peeves (cliffhanger, cliches, unlikeable heroine, contrived conflict), Colton and his drama penetrates and hooks. His aboutface will charm you, warm you, and make you care about what happens to him. I'd put up with the most unsavory of heroines just to spend more time with Ace.

4.5 "Spiderman. Batman. Superman. Ironman." "My spark." Kisses 
 So...I can't lie, I was mad at Colton when I read the last few paragraphs of 
 Driven 
 . Did the Prologue of Fueled make me feel a little shitty for that? Oh heck yes....but after I got through that, suffered through the emotional torment of Ryles and Colton...and then read the last few paragraphs of Fueled...I'm back to being pissed again! WTF K. Bromberg?!!?!? 
 Rylee Jade...damn it I love this girl. I want to hug her for about 5 minutes solid and then go out for drinks because she is so freakin relatable, it's scary. She's brave and sassy but still has that glimmer of insecurity and fear that all women have. She's compassionate and smart and freaking real. I connected with her even more over the course of this book. She just squeezed my heart so much, I felt every emotion, her happiness and glee, her sadness and devastation...it was such a rollercoaster, I'm mentally exhausted. She made me cry...almost as much as Colton did. I'm an emotional reader and when I connect with a heroine as much as I connected with Rylee, it's really hard for me to disconnect myself...so the entire tumultuous journey that she just experienced, I was right there with her, holding her hand. GAH!!! I just can't even tell you. 
 "I don't think I could ever get my fill of you." Proving my point exactly. Words that say it but don't really say it. "You're always so reserved, but when I'm in you..." he shakes his head, a low hum deep in his throat "...you lose all sense of everything, become mine, submit completely to me." 
 Colton FUCKIN Donavan...I dunno what to do with him. The prologue killed me. And then I went back and forth on my wonderful love-him-and-hate-him routine that I perfected during Driven. He is not an easy man to love, by any stretch of the imagination. But I will say having a glimpse at being inside his head was...helpful. Insightful. I liked it. Well, I didn't like it but...it was necessary to get to know why he does what he does. Being inside Colton's head was absolutely necessary in this book, there is no other way to hear and see some of the things that are needed, without being in his POV. You never knew when it was going to happen, it wasn't regular or routine, but it always made an impact. And understanding him more helped ease the pain on my heart just a little and okay...I'll admit it...I did love him more than I hated him. It's really impossible not to...even as exasperating as he can be. Until he did what I knew he was going to do and broke me just as quickly as he broke Rylee. 
 "I swear to God it's you!" 
 "Me?" I stutter flabbergasted. What did I have to do with what just happened? 
 "Mmm-hmm," he murmurs, staring at me intently. "I've never let my guard down. Never opened myself up to..." He shakes his head, his confusion and clarity written on his face. "I've been able to block things out for so long. Ignore emotions. Ignore everything, but you? You tear down walls I didn't even know I was building. You make me feel, Rylee." 
 Ace and Ryles...what can I say - don't read this book if you're of the faint of heart because it's a mother freakin angsty roller coaster of epic proportions. I'm happy, I'm sad, I'm ecstatic and then I wanna knee Colton in the balls (sound familiar? I said it in my Driven review too...I have a feeling that this is a reoccurring theme). I wanna fuck his brains out and then strangle him...yes, those familiar bi-polar crazy feelings are back in full force. I...was...all...over...the...place. I loved Rylee and Colton together...they're magic...they're this passionate burst of amazingness when they are together and happy. GOD BLESS AMERICA they are made for each other if that jack ass would just get it thru his head!!! GRRRR!!! (see...he's making me GRRR again!) I guess the part that makes me 'grrr' is the fact that Colton is his own worst enemy. There is one thing stopping Rylee and Colton from being amazing together...and that's Colton and his past. Not that his past isn't a minefield of fucked up and he has every right to feel the way he does but he's fucking up one of the few good things in his life and Rylee is SO amazingly awesome...I cannot fathom them not being together. And if he only knew how much Rylee could help him...if he only let her. 
 "Stop." His voice is stern, and I can't help but look up to meet his bemused eyes. "Look, I don't know how to explain it." His voice softens and he shakes his head. "I can't really. All I know it that with you, things were just different from the start. You broke the mold, Rylee." 
 There are a lot of skeletons that get revealed in this book...a few more from Rylee that I wasn't expecting and we start to see more and more from Colton and his horrible past, which obviously needed to happen. Badly. The only way for both of them to move forward is complete honesty...on both sides and I really liked that. And then Rylee goes and does something insanely stupid. I screamed, I cried, I stopped reading. The second I read it, I dropped my kindle and almost refused to continue. Because I knew what was going to happen next...and it did...and I cried more...and it sucked. For the next 25%+ it SUCKED. Ripped my heart out, stomped on it and drug me along for a painful suckville ride. It wasn't pretty...I didn't know if I was going to survive. 
 "Just remember what I always say; don't lose yourself trying to hold onto someone who doesn't care about losing you." 
 I love angsty books, I've said this over and over...and this part of the book was probably one of the most angsty books I've read. The entire time I am warring with myself because I know the truth, but I see Rylee's point and I'm CHEERING her on because she's being so smart and standing up for herself but at the cost of her fuckin spirit. She loves him so much. SO much it makes me tear up thinking about it. And I know he loves her, as much as his fucked up little heart can. Them together is brilliance written on paper and the torture of them being apart cannot be fully expressed in words. They're both shell's of the people they could be when they are apart...hence my total devastation. I just can't even begin to tell you the pain that was inflicted on my soul...I might never recover from it. It was beautiful torture but it still fuckin hurts. 
 '"I might not be able to tell you the things you need to hear with the traditional words you need to hear them in, but I swear to God, Rylee, I will try. And if I can't, then I'll show you. I'll show you with everything I have - anything it takes - where you place is in my life," he murmurs to me, shattering every last form of protection I have guarding my heart. 
 He just stole it completely. 
 And I just more than willingly handed it over.' 
 So after I've cried I dunno how many times, I'm just begging for someone to kill them or me or both...or maybe I'll just climb into the book and commit murder/suicide....thats when it happens. I love Kristen Ashley's writing. Whenever I'm in the mood for that alpha male hero - even if they are just shy of being an anti-hero, or, in this case, if they are a centuries old vampire, I know that I can count on Kristen to provide that character. She does not disappoint with Lucien, and in fact, really delivered a new type of Vampire for me to love. I'm not an avid paranormal reader, so I don't know if my standards are as high as others that consider that their main genre, but Lucien is definitely one to remember. 
 This story starts off with Leah attending her Selection. Her family has been offering its members up, for generations, to be concubines to Vampires. This was an agreement settled upon between vampires and mortals in order to provide some type of order and rule to Vampires feeding off of humans. Leah is not happy about her fate, and she has further tried to avoid that fate by continuing to be in a relationship since coming of age, as they will not take a man or woman from a known relationship. So, this is another factor that I liked about Leah - she was 40 and not that young, naive female character that does not know her mind. 
 Lucien, who is somewhat of a legend among his people, has been waiting for Leah since she came of age to be in a Selection, so everyone knows that she belongs to him. Everyone except for Leah, that is. She fights this for weeks, which Lucien actually appreciates and looks forward to, as he feels that the agreement has taken away something elemental from Vampires - the ability to hunt and "tame" a mate of their choosing. So, without asking anyone, Lucien actually creates a different type of arrangement with Leah, and this sets off a domino effect within the world of Vampires, as well as other Immortals. It actually begins a set of Prophecies, although more is to be revealed in the coming books. 
 As for Lucien and Leah, there are many among Lucien's kind that are against Lucien having the type of relationship with Leah that he wishes to have, so they set about making life difficult for Leah, as she is the most fragile of the two. Lucien finds out that he has more people supporting him, however, than he realized, but he has to find out who he can and can't trust before Leah is hurt.

There are two ways to read this book. One way is to listen when Ashley speaks via her hero and says 'Don't judge this by human morals.' She makes it clear that this vampiric species is humanity's natural predator and that the concubine/vampire relationship is actually a form of protection for the human race. Since the concubines provide food for the vampires and are protected by the tenets of vampiric culture, vampires aren't allowed to go hunting for humans. Looked at in this way, the concubine/vampire relationship, on paper, makes sense. However, the other way to read this book is with human morals. If you look at Lucien's and Leah's relationship with ideas like 'free will' and the right to say no in mind, it's rather disturbing. With regards to Leah, the thought of Stockholm Syndrome came to mind at several points and if I'd be in Leah's exact shoes, I'm pretty sure I would have gone catatonic. 
 I was perpetually straddling the line between objective reader and outraged woman. If Ashley were to strip this story of all its paranormal elements, Lucien would be so far from a hero, it's not funny. He stalks her for years, forces her to sign herself into indentured servitude, isolates her from her friends and family, strips her of her ability to choose, and is borderline emotionally/physically abusive. Ashley even admits in the book that if the vampire Ruling Council found out that Lucien forced Leah into the contract, he'd be punished. So, in that respect, you can't claim it's a cultural thing because even the vampires think it's wrong! 
 I do think this was one of Ashley's strongest examples of world-building. If she had chosen to go more of a 'marriage of convenience' route, where Leah knew what she was getting herself into, it would have been a much stronger book. Lucien, despite being his asshole tendencies, was a consistent character. He never changed who he was, but as Leah fell in love with him (I still don't understand why), the stronger connection to her made him dial back the asshole-ness. Leah, on the other hand, was all over the place. She's forty-years old, but has the maturity level of a twenty-year old. She's strong-willed and she makes some monumentally bad decisions. If she hadn't gotten expelled from Vampire Studies, she would have known her contract was unusual and she could have been free of Lucien right away. She was a media specialist, for cripes sake. Maybe that means something different in the UK, but for me, that means she was a school librarian and nobody knows the power of information more than librarians.
